blinding_guess.why: The parameter base name is derived as base_topic.substr(get_effective_namespace().length()) with '/' replaced by '.' (compressed_publisher.cpp:144-146). This yields camera.image_raw.compressed.* only when the node is in the root namespace '/'. For a node in a non-root namespace such as '/ns', the separating '/' after the namespace is not removed, so the names would start with '.', and a base topic not under the node's namespace would be cut at an arbitrary character. The names of the listed parameters therefore depend on how get_effective_namespace is used, and that use looks fragile.

notes: Parameter names are partly built at run time. The package declares '<param_base_name>.compressed.<descriptor name>', where param_base_name is base_topic with its first get_effective_namespace().length() characters removed and '/' replaced by '.' (compressed_publisher.cpp:144-149, 381-382). The packet names match base topic '/camera/image_raw' published from a node whose effective namespace is '/'. The suffix 'compressed.<name>', the types, the defaults and the ranges are fixed in code, so the three params are recorded under declares with the packet names. Static values: format string, default "jpeg", additional_constraints 'Supported values: [jpeg, png, tiff]'; png_level PARAMETER_INTEGER, default 3, range 0..9 step 1; jpeg_quality PARAMETER_INTEGER, default 95, range 1..100 step 1 (the comment at line 85 says 0 to 100). All three have read_only false. The publisher also declares jpeg_compress_bayer (bool), tiff.res_unit (string), tiff.xdpi and tiff.ydpi (int); none of these is a packet element. The subscriber plugin makes the same get_effective_namespace call (compressed_subscriber.cpp:83-85) and declares '<base>.compressed.mode' (string, default "unchanged"). QoS, rate and definition_id are null for all ports because the elements are parameters and a C++ API call, not topics or message definitions. No dependency definition files were fetched and definition_hash.py was not needed. The cfg/CompressedPublisher.cfg and cfg/CompressedSubscriber.cfg files are ROS 1 dynamic_reconfigure definitions with different defaults (jpeg_quality 80 in 1..100, png_level 9 in 1..9). CMakeLists.txt does not build them (ament_cmake, no dynamic_reconfigure), so they are not taken as this revision's ROS 2 interface. The snapshot also holds the sibling packages of the image_transport_plugins repository (compressed_depth, theora, zstd). They appeared in a snapshot-wide search for the element names but are not part of this package and are not described.
